Q: C++26 constant_wrapper and constant_arg_t A:

Update: In the March 2026 meeting, P3948 was adopted, which removes std::constant_arg<f> from the standard library and replaces all usage of it with std::constant_wrapper<f>.

The issue is that there is a potential ambiguity between the tag treatment and std::constant_wrapper, in a rather contrived scenario.

std::constant_wrapper has a call operator, and the semantics of std::cw<F>(X) are to yield std::cw<F(decltype(X)::value)>. It might change to conditionally just do F(X) as as well (see P3987R2), but let's stick with the wrapped version for now (and the existence of the unwrapping call operator doesn't affect this reasoning).

What if you have an F and an X that potentially behave differently based on wrapping behavior?

// Simply check if there is a V::value
inline constexpr F = []<class V>(V v) -> bool {
    return requires { V::value; };
};

struct Answer { static constexpr int value = 42; };
inline constexpr Answer answer;

Now, std::cw<F>(answer) is std::cw<F(Answer::value)> is std::cw<false>. We unwrap on the way into the call, so since we invoke F with just an int, that's false — but it's a wrapped false.

But what is std::function_ref<bool(Answer)>(std::cw<F>)(answer)? Is this:

  • treating cw<F> as a tag that we're initializing the funcion_ref with F in a non-dangling way? In this case, we're treating F as the callable, and F(answer) is true.
  • treating cw<F> as a callable that satisfies the signature bool(Answer)? In this case, we're treating cw<F> as the callable, and cw<F>(answer) is cw<false>, which converts to false.

We got different answers depending on our interpretation.

Note that other call wrappers don't have this tagged treatment, so std::function<bool(Answer)>(cw<F>)(answer) is false. So function_ref<Sig>(cw<F>) could behave differently from all other call wrappers (function, copyable_function, move_only_function).

But this really only happens when you have some callable such that f(x) and f(cw<x>) are both valid and have different behavior.

With constant_arg, there's only one possible treatment, so there's no ambiguity in this sense.

Q: NSMetadataQuery not returning relevant files A:

I realized that just disabling the app sandbox was not enough. It does help when accessing some files beneath the home directory, but not everywhere. E.g. the code above returned files within ~/Library and ~/Photos.

However, if you want to get results from ~/Documents you still need to give full disk access to your application via Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk access. Drag&Drop your development app bundle from DerivedData. Disabling the app sandbox is not enough.

Of course, if you need this in a production build, you need to guide the user to do that.

Q: Adding custom view to navigation with Liquid Glass effect like Connect App A:

Regarding the first point:

The chips have some weird background color

The background is the translucent effect that you get with .regular glass, which is the default. There is also a shadow effect with this kind of glass.

To make the items more transparent, try using .clear glass instead. There is no shadow effect with clear glass either. If you are intending to add tap gestures to the items, you might want to make the glass interactive too:

.glassEffect(.clear.interactive())

Regarding the second point:

Scrolling the list up makes it fade out below the navigation, but the chips are not taken into account

If you want the fade effect to start behind your glassy items, you just need to change it from .safeAreaInset to .safeAreaBar. The documentation has a discussion:

Similar to the safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) modifier, the content view is anchored to the specified horizontal edge of the parent view and its width insets the safe area.

Additionally, it extends the edge effect of any scroll views affected by the inset safe area.

.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) {
    ScrollView(.horizontal) {
        // ...
    }
}

Q: Round a divided number in Bash A:

One can use floating point arithmetic with bc, add 0.5 for the rounding and take away what is after the comma:

echo '3/2 + 0.5' | bc -l | sed 's/\..*//'

Q: (Solved) Debian / Apache + Virtual Hosts / PHP-FPM: PHP files loaded from wrong directory A:

It's not allowed to use the "doc_root" ini setting in "php.ini".

Well: The PHP documentation regarding this setting is rather misleading. It says:

"if PHP was not compiled with FORCE_REDIRECT, you SHOULD set doc_root if you are running php as a CGI under any web server"

I followed this advice, only to land at a nonfunctional virtual server setup.
Commenting out doc_root (thus restoring the original state, ignoring what the documentation states about "php as a CGI under any web server") leads to a functioning system.
The advice seems to be simply wrong (outdated?).
